Excellent steak in Hanoi - not cheap but worth it!
Sep 2026 • Family
Keen to break the diet of Vietnamese food with some red meat, we had a family meal here to indulge our steak desire! It is very good indeed - the meat is very well sourced, and the rest of the menu is varied and all high quality. The service was a little over the top (a common western reaction, perhaps), but very charming. It was very empty when we went, despite the city being full on a public holiday, so I hope the place is not struggling financially. It deserves to succeed - it was really a very good meal, and reasonably priced (by western standards) for such good cooking.

Disappointing
Dec 2020
I think this restaurant is trying to be something it just doesn't have the talent to be.

Food: ingredients are good, but the restaurant doesn't know what to do with them. Grilled steak is supposed to have some char: ours didn't. The chimichurri didn't taste anything like an Argentinian chimmi is supposed to taste and the side dishes (e.g. dry creamed spinach) were bland and mediocre. 

Service isn't inattentive; it's just insensitive. Our server literally took the appetizer plate away from my wife while she was using it! They also left us a salad bowl with no serving tongs (server took those away too) and were generally crowding us and not paying attention to what we were doing.

The place is pretty but there are better options in Hanoi for the price.

Superior Experience and Delicious Food
Mar 2019 • Friends
You won't find yourself at Rico if you're looking for an inexpensive meal. However, if you do go, and I do think you should, you'll hopefully be as pleased as we were. The ambiance is quite cozy and has the feel of classical (frankly, colonial Hanoi). The staff were immediately welcoming and warm. Heck, even the motorbike guard was really friendly and welcoming! From the beginning, I was impressed by the service here. The staff was patient and was obviously trying to ensure that we ordered meals that we'd like. They encouraged us not to over-order but we did anyway! I really liked the iPad-based menu. Somehow, the pictures helped us order our starters and sides. We already knew (and had pre-ordered) our beef Wellingtons. From beginning to end, the staff paid attention to us but was never intrusive. I will say that one of our party ordered his beef Wellington medium rather than the standard medium rare. His came out medium rare like the rest of us. The wait staff offered to take it back and cook it more. 

Overall, this was a really enjoyable grown-ups night out. Yes, it was pricy. It was by far the most expensive meal we've had in our six months in Hanoi. But, this was a special event and we all thoroughly enjoyed it.

Rubber Wrapped in Dough
Jan 2019 • Family
Four of us went to Rico for a birthday celebration, we'd ordered the beef Wellington a day ahead as a favorite. Two of us shared this. The beef Wellington itself, medium rare, looked fantastic, a bit brown on the outside, dripping red in the middle, as the waiter who cut ours into pieces was proud to show. Which was amazing for a piece of rubber coated and cooked in dough. Later, seeing the uneaten meat on our plates, she asked us how our meal was. We told her the truth, calmly. She asked us to write what we'd said on a sheet of paper, which we did, "rubber." Google helped us translate this into Vietnamese. She took our plates away, largely uneaten -- the food, not the plates. Three of us ordered deserts. Why not, we were still hungry. Then she brought a complimentary desert for the birthday person, who was thus treated or threatened with a second desert. "Threatened" only to the extent that my own desert, a tarte tatin, was still cold in the middle, probably from the freezer. You think they might have given us an idea that the birthday person might not also order a desert? The bill came, more than USD 200. We thought, at a minimum, they'd comp a desert given the nearly VND 800,000 for the blood red dripping rubber impersonation of steak... or maybe even not charge us for the "thing" served to us. But no, each item was well itemized, in full. The waiter explained that the rubber was from Argentina, and the one good steak we did order, and enjoy, was apparently other than from an Argentinian rubber plantation. We've enjoyed Rico since its opening. We've enjoyed the ambiance, service and food. You know the "death and taxes" thing -- good times end.
